chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'When a woman dies, who is most rightful in offering the funeral prayer (Salat) upon her?' He said, 'Her husband.' I said, 'Is the husband more rightful than the father, the son, and the brother?' He said, 'Yes, and he washes her.'

key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهَا: He washes her (ritual bathing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: Who has the primary right to perform the funeral prayer for a deceased woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the juridical hierarchy for performing the funeral prayer (*Salat al-Janazah*) and washing the body (*Ghusl*) of a deceased woman, establishing the husband as the primary heir to these duties over male agnates like the father and son. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the husband's unique role as the head of the household and primary guardian, distinguishing his rights from those of the paternal lineage. The emphasis on the husband washing her body underscores the intimacy and responsibility inherent in the marital bond within Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘The woman dies, who would be the most rightful with the praying of the Salaat upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘Her husband’. I said, ‘The husband is more rightful than the father, and the son, and the brother?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, and he can wash her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-ffusayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir from who has said the following: “

I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who is the most deserving to perform Salah (prayer) for a deceased woman? He (the Imam) said, ‘It is her husband.’ I then asked, ‘Is her husband more deserving or her father, son or brother? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, her husband is more deserving.’”
